clean_source_blocks.text: The US-Iran memorandum of understanding announced on Wednesday amounts to a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and a deal to try to reach a final deal on almost everything else. President Donald Trump framed it as a major win for the US in a lengthy press conference at the G7 summit in France. But new details released by US officials in a call with reporters confirm both countries still have a long way to go to reach a comprehensive final peace agreement that achieves Trump's primary goal of stopping Iran from ever developing nuclear weapons. Trump has insisted the deal ensures that Iran will never buy, develop or produce a nuclear weapon. But the text of this agreement, which was read aloud by officials on the call, falls short of that.
Trump has insisted the deal ensures that Iran will never buy, develop or produce a nuclear weapon. But text of the agreement falls short of that.

Donald Trump says the US agreement with Iran will be signed "shortly" and could be done tomorrow, as US officials reveal details of the deal The 14-paragraph agreement says Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, and also commits to a $300bn fund for the "reconstruction and economic development" of the country - although the US is not required to contribute The agreement declares the "immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts, including in Lebanon" And it says the US and Iran "commit to negotiating and achieving the final deal in maximum 60 days, extendable with mutual consent". Read the key points of the deal here Donald Trump earlier warned the deal - which was scheduled to be formally signed on Friday - is "not final"

Trump has also said the US will not provide any money to Iran. This is a key issue for the president, who has been critical of the Obama administration's $1.7 billion payment to Iran in 2016. With an eye toward his legacy, Trump has been keen to frame his Iran deal as better than former President Barack Obama's, and has used the money issue as a way to argue he has taken a stronger stance against Tehran. But according to the text of this agreement, the US will work "with regional partners to develop a definitive mutually agreed plan with at least USD $300 billion" for Iran's reconstruction.

[Lähde: BBC World]
The US-Iran memorandum of understanding announced on Wednesday amounts to a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and a deal to try to reach a final deal on almost everything else.

President Donald Trump framed it as a major win for the US in a lengthy press conference at the G7 summit in France.

But new details released by US officials in a call with reporters confirm both countries still have a long way to go to reach a comprehensive final peace agreement that achieves Trump's primary goal of stopping Iran from ever developing nuclear weapons.

Trump has insisted the deal ensures that Iran will never buy, develop or produce a nuclear weapon. But the text of this agreement, which was read aloud by officials on the call, falls short of that.

Instead, the ceasefire extension jumpstarts a high-stakes scramble over 60 days for the two adversaries to achieve a lasting nuclear pact. It took the Obama administration 20 months of negotiations to reach the original Iran nuclear deal in 2015. Can the Trump administration do that in just two months?

For now, the text of the deal only commits Iran to "downblending" its stockpile of highly enriched uranium, under the supervision of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). A senior US official on Wednesday called it a "significant concession" by Iran.

But all of the technical details of how that might happen, and on what timeline, must still be ironed out in the 60-day period of negotiations that commence after the scheduled signing takes place on Friday.

Trump has also said the US will not provide any money to Iran. This is a key issue for the president, who has been critical of the Obama administration's $1.7 billion payment to Iran in 2016.

With an eye toward his legacy, Trump has been keen to frame his Iran deal as better than former President Barack Obama's, and has used the money issue as a way to argue he has taken a stronger stance against Tehran.

But according to the text of this agreement, the US will work "with regional partners to develop a definitive mutually agreed plan with at least USD $300 billion" for Iran's reconstruction.

A senior US official said the deal does not commit the US to paying Iran a single cent. But the actual language in the agreement is opaque, and appears to leave the door open for the US to eventually make some payments to Iran as part of a negotiated settlement to the war.

payload.title: Yhdysvaltain ja Iranin alustava sopu jättää ratkaisevat kysymykset auki
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltain ja Iranin alustava yhteisymmärrys avaisi Hormuzinsalmen uudelleen ja lopettaisi sotatoimet, mutta varsinainen lopullinen sopimus on määrä neuvotella vasta seuraavien 60 päivän aikana.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain ja Iranin keskiviikkona julkistettu alustava yhteisymmärrys avaisi Hormuzinsalmen uudelleen ja käynnistäisi neuvottelut lopullisesta sopimuksesta. Presidentti Donald Trump on kuvannut järjestelyä merkittäväksi voitoksi, mutta Yhdysvaltain viranomaisten esiin tuomat yksityiskohdat osoittavat, että moni keskeinen kysymys on yhä ratkaisematta.

## Alustava sopu ei vielä ole lopullinen

Trump sanoi G7-huippukokouksen yhteydessä Ranskassa, että Yhdysvaltain ja Iranin sopimus allekirjoitetaan pian ja että se voisi tapahtua jo seuraavana päivänä. Hän kuitenkin varoitti aiemmin, ettei järjestely ole vielä lopullinen.

Viranomaisten mukaan 14-kohtainen sopimusteksti toteaa, ettei Iranilla tule koskaan olemaan ydinasetta. Trump on sanonut sopimuksen varmistavan, ettei Iran koskaan osta, kehitä tai valmista ydinasetta. Julki luetun tekstin perusteella järjestely ei kuitenkaan vielä yksin saavuta tätä tavoitetta, vaan maat sitoutuvat neuvottelemaan lopullisen sopimuksen enintään 60 päivän kuluessa. Määräaikaa voidaan jatkaa yhteisellä suostumuksella.

Sopimusluonnos sisältää myös kirjauksen sotatoimien välittömästä ja pysyvästä päättämisestä kaikilla rintamilla, mukaan lukien Libanonissa. Tässä vaiheessa kyse on silti ennen kaikkea kehyksestä, jonka varaan laajempi rauhansopimus yritetään rakentaa.

## Rahasto ja jälleenrakennus herättävät kysymyksiä

Yksi merkittävä yksityiskohta liittyy Iranin jälleenrakennukseen ja taloudelliseen kehitykseen. Sopimusteksti sitoo osapuolet vähintään 300 miljardin dollarin rahastoon Iranin jälleenrakennusta ja taloudellista kehitystä varten. Yhdysvaltojen ei kuitenkaan edellytetä maksavan rahastoon.

Trump on erikseen korostanut, ettei Yhdysvallat anna Iranille rahaa. Tämä on hänelle poliittisesti keskeinen kysymys, sillä hän on arvostellut Barack Obaman hallinnon vuonna 2016 Iranille tekemää 1,7 miljardin dollarin maksua. Nyt esillä olevan tekstin mukaan Yhdysvallat toimisi alueellisten kumppanien kanssa sellaisen suunnitelman laatimiseksi, josta osapuolet voisivat sopia.

Alustava yhteisymmärrys voi siten vähentää välitöntä jännitystä ja avata reitin laajempaan ratkaisuun. Samalla se jättää avoimeksi juuri ne kysymykset, joiden perusteella sopimuksen todellinen merkitys lopulta arvioidaan.
summary_bullets: Alustava yhteisymmärrys tähtää Hormuzinsalmen avaamiseen ja sotatoimien päättämiseen.
Lopullinen sopimus on määrä neuvotella enintään 60 päivän aikana, ellei jatkosta sovita.
Sopimusteksti puhuu vähintään 300 miljardin dollarin jälleenrakennusrahastosta, mutta Yhdysvaltojen ei edellytetä maksavan siihen.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketissa annettuihin BBC:n lähdetietoihin. Keskeiset avoimet kohdat on esitetty varovaisesti, koska kyse on alustavasta yhteisymmärryksestä eikä lopullisesta sopimuksesta.

Donald Trump says the US agreement with Iran will be signed "shortly" and could be done tomorrow, as US officials reveal details of the deal The 14-paragraph agreement says Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, and also commits to a $300bn fund for the "reconstruction and economic development" of the country - although the US is not required to contribute The agreement declares the "immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts, including in Lebanon" And it says the US and Iran "commit to negotiating and achieving the final deal in maximum 60 days, extendable with mutual consent". Read the key points of the deal here Donald Trump earlier warned the deal - which was scheduled to be formally signed on Friday - is "not final"

Trump has also said the US will not provide any money to Iran. This is a key issue for the president, who has been critical of the Obama administration's $1.7 billion payment to Iran in 2016. With an eye toward his legacy, Trump has been keen to frame his Iran deal as better than former President Barack Obama's, and has used the money issue as a way to argue he has taken a stronger stance against Tehran. But according to the text of this agreement, the US will work "with regional partners to develop a definitive mutually agreed plan with at least USD $300 billion" for Iran's reconstruction.
